text: Long Nights, Eddie Vedder, and it is one. Just me, the anchor light and a gull pretending to be asleep.
Coffee on, Opa grumbling, the bay going pale. The Velvet Underground and Nico, Sunday Morning, whatever day it actually is.
Somewhere round the middle of the night on the Zeemeeuw. Red Hot Chili Peppers, Midnight. Gerrit's asleep in his crate, so we keep it down.
Snow on the wheelhouse roof, and Gerrit glaring at it from his crate. Dead and Company, Cold Rain and Snow, ten minutes live. For once a song title knows what it's talking about.
Cold rain on the glass, no snow yet. Dead and Company, Cold Rain and Snow. Half the title's come true. I'll take it.
Spring out here means the gulls get loud and Gerrit gets ideas. The Zombies, Time of the Season.
Not a cloud up there, only a vapour trail or two heading somewhere I'm not. Jack Johnson, Traffic in the Sky.
The wind's throwing spray right over the bow, so here's the Manic Street Preachers with Ocean Spray. [dryly] Very method.
In a wind like this, Gerrit doesn't fly away so much as get relocated. Lenny Kravitz, Fly Away.
Fog all round. Can't see the lighthouse, can't see the ferry. Only the Ocean, Jack Johnson, and not much of that either.
Burner on, both hands round the mug, the wheelhouse windows steamed up from the inside. The Doors, Light My Fire, all seven minutes. It's that kind of winter.
Opa's sulking, the aerial's rattling, and the repair can wait till this blows over. Stereophonics, Maybe Tomorrow.
